title: Automate benchmark-lab runs across regions (orchestration, retries, artifact storage)
creator: Claire Dubois
description:
Context
We need a repeatable way to run the latency-per-dollar benchmark suite in multiple Redwood regions with consistent config, bounded impact on production, and deterministic artifact outputs for downstream QA + marketing table generation.

Right now, region runs are partially manual (kick off region-by-region, copy artifacts, hand-check failures). This creates two problems:
1) Inconsistency risk (different flags/config drift, different warmups, different retry behavior)
2) Operational load (hard to schedule within the SRE capacity windows and keep runs aligned)

Goal
Add a region-runner/orchestrator to benchmark-lab that:
- Executes the same benchmark suite across an explicit list of regions
- Enforces the same config (workload spec, concurrency, seq length distro, caching/warmup policy)
- Handles transient failures with controlled retries (no infinite loops)
- Stores artifacts per region in a predictable layout (for QC + report build)
- Produces a single aggregated summary artifact (manifest + per-region metrics) for review/sign-off

Non-goals
- Building a fully general workflow scheduler (we can trigger via CI/manual runbook initially)
- Changing benchmark methodology (that lives in the methodology doc / ENG-2841 output schema)
- Publishing artifacts publicly (this is internal storage + sanitized export handled by the public table pipeline)

Constraints / dependencies
- Must respect SRE capacity windows per region (see confluence: benchmark run capacity window plan). Runner should accept a window token/identifier and tag artifacts with it.
- Must integrate with guardrails/canary gating so we can stop if production risk is detected (ENG-2895).
- Output schema must include the latency/$ metric and existing run metadata (ENG-2841).

Proposed design
CLI entrypoint
- Add `benchmark-lab region-run` command.
- Inputs:
  - `--regions us-east-1,us-west-2,eu-central-1,ap-southeast-1` (explicit list)
  - `--suite <name>` (e.g., `latency_per_dollar_v1_chat`, `latency_per_dollar_v1_embeddings`)
  - `--config <path>` (yaml/json with method-approved knobs)
  - `--artifacts-uri gs://redwood-benchmarks/<env>/` (or s3 equivalent)
  - `--window-id <string>` (capacity window ID from SRE plan)
  - `--max-retries N` (default 2) + `--retry-backoff-seconds` (default 60) + jitter
  - `--fail-fast` optional (default false; we want best-effort across regions but with clear summary)

Execution model
- Sequential per region by default (to reduce cross-region load + simplify capacity coordination). Optional parallelism behind a flag, gated by SRE.
- For each region:
  - Validate region is allowed for this suite (prevent typo -> wrong/unsupported region).
  - Validate required headers/options are set for region selection (matches Redwood API routing behavior).
  - Run warmup phase (per methodology) then measurement window.
  - Collect raw outputs + summary stats.
  - Upload artifacts to `.../<suite>/<window-id>/<timestamp>/<region>/...`

Retry policy (transient-only)
- Retry on:
  - 429/503 from the inference endpoint
  - network timeouts
  - artifact upload transient failures
- Do not retry on:
  - schema validation errors
  - missing/invalid config
  - guardrail trip (abort entire run)
- On retry, re-run the full region job (not partial) and record attempt number in manifest.

Artifact layout (deterministic)
- Per-run root:
  - `manifest.json` (region list, config hash, git sha, tool version, start/end timestamps, window-id)
  - `aggregate_summary.json` (table-like summary across regions; same schema used by QC notes)
- Per-region:
  - `raw_results.jsonl` (or existing raw output format)
  - `metrics.json` (p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost/1M, latency/$ + any confidence/variance summary if available)
  - `runner_logs.txt`
  - `env.json` (region, instance type if applicable, runtime flags snapshot, sdk version)

Observability + safety
- Emit structured logs with region + attempt fields.
- Hook into guardrails endpoint/checks from ENG-2895 (or stub: callout to a `guardrails_check()` that can be wired in).
- If guardrails trip in any region: stop remaining regions, mark run as ABORTED, upload partial manifest.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Running a single command produces artifacts for all requested regions with identical config hash.
- [ ] Manifest includes: suite name, region list, tool git SHA, config hash, window-id, start/end timestamps, per-region status (success/failed/aborted) and attempt counts.
- [ ] Retries occur only for transient categories; retries are bounded and visible.
- [ ] A rerun with same inputs produces the same artifact structure (different timestamp folder is OK).
- [ ] Aggregated summary is machine-readable and aligns with ENG-2841 output schema.
- [ ] SRE review sign-off: sequential default + explicit opt-in for parallel.

Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - retry classifier (what errors qualify)
  - manifest writer + schema validation
  - artifact path formatter
- Integration test (staging):
  - run 2 regions with small suite + force one transient failure to validate retry

Rollout plan
- Phase 1: Manual invocation during scheduled windows (runbook-driven), artifacts stored in internal bucket.
- Phase 2: CI job wrapper for nightly/weekly scheduled runs (still gated by capacity windows).

Open questions
- Should we enforce a max wall-clock per region to avoid overrunning a window? (suggest yes; default 90 min, configurable)
- Artifact backend: we currently assume GCS in prod tooling—confirm if we need S3 compatibility for on-prem/private test envs.

Links
- Benchmark scope + success metrics: PM-418
- Guardrails + stop conditions: ENG-2895
- Latency/$ output schema: ENG-2841
- Capacity windows plan: Confluence (SRE capacity planning / benchmark run window plan)

Owner notes
This ticket is intentionally narrow: get multi-region orchestration, retries, and artifact storage done in a way that’s boring and auditable. We can iterate on scheduling/parallelism after launch if needed.
comments: 2025-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): Default must be sequential. If we add parallelism, require explicit `--parallel` and a hard cap (e.g., 2 regions) + only within approved windows. Also ensure we have an abort hook if region health degrades.
2025-02-05 (Neha Kapoor): Please wire in the guardrails check as a first-class stop condition. If it trips, we should not ‘best-effort’ continue other regions.
2025-02-07 (Claire Dubois): Artifact layout looks good; please ensure config hash includes *all* methodology-sensitive knobs. We got burned last quarter with hidden defaults drifting.

2025-02-11 (Rina Kobayashi): Implementation in progress on branch `region-runner`. Planning to reuse existing suite runner and wrap per-region execution with manifest + uploader. Will add retry classifier + bounded attempts.
2025-02-14 (Vanessa Ortiz): Capacity windows: APAC window is tight. A per-region max wall-clock will help us avoid overruns. Please include timestamps in manifest for each region start/end.

2025-02-17 (Rina Kobayashi): PR up for review (benchmark-lab: region runner orchestration). Added deterministic artifact paths + manifest, sequential default, bounded retry. Need SRE sign-off on stop conditions + default timeouts.
